item.title: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format
item.description: arXiv:2611.03859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a preconditioning pipeline that accelerates Tensor Train (TT) linear solvers for symmetric positive-definite problems. Extending the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, we construct a preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose. This formulation is positive semidefinite for any bond dimension and truncation, and definite whenever the factor is non-singular, satisfying the mathematical requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. We detail the construction of this preconditioner and its integration into Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)-like linear solvers. Performance evaluations show consistent iteration reductions for anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems across various configurations, leading to net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned settings of time stepping schemes that can reuse the approximate inverses. These benchmarks were performed with the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl, which we also introduce in this work to provide out-of-the-box access to these preconditioned pipelines.
item.dc:creator: Pau Torrente Badia, Daniel P\'erez Garc\'ia, Artur Garcia-Saez, Stefano Carignano

item.title: Weighted Randomized Kaczmarz for Sparsely Corrupted Linear Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalized weighted randomized Kaczmarz framework to approximate solutions to overdetermined linear systems whose measurements are perturbed by sparse, additive corruptions. The proposed framework samples equations with probabilities proportional to a user-defined weighting function of their corresponding residual magnitudes. Our work focuses on weighting functions that will reduce the influence of potentially corrupted equations, and provides analyses for a general class of non-increasing weighting functions. We derive one-step expected squared error bounds that separate progress on uncorrupted equations from the contribution of corrupted equations, and provide sufficient conditions for geometric convergence under one specific family of weighting functions -- threshold weighting. We also investigate adaptive exponential weights scaled by the median or median absolute deviation of residual magnitudes, requiring no prior knowledge of the corruption fraction or magnitudes. Lastly, we consider a family of inverse residual weighting functions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefit of such a generalized framework in its flexibility in developing approaches for settings in which information about the corruptions is known or unknown.
item.dc:creator: Jessie Chen, Ziyu Cheng, Yunhui He, Alona Kryshchenko, Jocelyn T. Chi, Anna Ma, Jamie Haddock

item.title: A probabilistic score estimation using the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.03915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Score-learning methods generally lack pointwise supervision, which affects the training accuracy, particularly in regions where SDE trajectories are rare. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel method called \emph{BEL anchors}, which uses Monte Carlo score estimates at user-selected space-time query points. By combining a Feynman--Kac representation of the Fokker--Planck equation with the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula, our estimator requires neither closed-form transition densities, spatial discretization, nor derivatives of the initial density. We derive its asymptotic variance and use the anchors as sparse supervised targets for existing score-learning objectives. Experiments show that BEL anchors improve implicit score matching in poorly sampled regions, prevent score-PINN collapse, and enable accurate sample regeneration in several numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Jiatong Sun, Long Nguyen, Ning Jiang, Weiqi Chu, Yao Li

item.title: Initial-Trace Insufficiency and Entropy-Accounting Separation in Finite-Volume Coarse Graining
item.description: arXiv:2611.04001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coarse finite-volume information does not automatically define an exact pathwise closure for the restricted evolution of a fine-grid realization. We study two one-step information boundaries that are distinct from recursive predictive memory. First, we show that parent averages together with complete initial parent-interface trace pairs are sufficient for one forward-Euler finite-volume transition with a deterministic two-state numerical flux, but they do not generally determine a completed second-order strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta, equivalently Heun, transition. An explicit scalar upwind collision shows that hidden interior data can affect later stage traces and hence the completed parent update, even when initial traces and parent averages agree. Second, we show that exact conservative one-step closure is not the same as entropy-accounting closure. A parent entropy balance obtained from a cellwise numerical entropy balance contains a subcell Jensen gap, a realized entropy-flux difference, and residual dissipation. For a declared Burgers-Rusanov conservative flux and a declared Rusanov-type numerical entropy flux, we construct a sign-indexed finite family in which all branches have identical parent averages, identical conservative interface registers, and identical next parent averages, while the entropy-interface register distinguishes every branch. Under the uniform branch law, the conservative channel leaves nonzero deterministic squared-error floors for both the raw entropy register and its cyclic divergence. The results give a concise finite-volume information-sufficiency test for multistage interface data and entropy-side accounting.
item.dc:creator: Antonis Polemitis (UNIC Evolve, University of Nicosia, Nicosia, Cyprus), Nicholas Christakis (Institute for Advanced Modelling and Simulation, University of Nicosia, Nicosia, Cyprus), Dimitris Drikakis (Institute for Advanced Modelling and Simulation, University of Nicosia, Nicosia, Cyprus)

item.title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.
item.dc:creator: Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo

item.title: Adaptive data-driven reduced-order models for reciprocal MIMO port-Hamiltonian dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems provide a general framework for modeling a broad class of physical dynamical systems, including systems with dissipation. Constructing accurate and robust data-driven reduced-order models for general pH systems is challenging. In this work, we focus on an important subclass of pH systems satisfying reciprocity, a property arising naturally in a variety of models. Rather than seeking to preserve the full pH structure, we exploit the additional symmetry provided by reciprocity to develop an efficient data-driven reduced-order modeling approach. We show that every minimal realization of a reciprocal system is self-adjoint with respect to a generally indefinite inner product and can, up to a similarity transformation preserving the pH structure, be represented in a Krein space with a signature inner product. This observation motivates a Galerkin projection onto a tangential rational Krylov subspace with respect to the corresponding indefinite inner product. Although the resulting projection involves full-order state solutions and the unknown inner product, we show that its reduced mass and stiffness matrices can be constructed directly from transfer-function data through a Loewner formulation. We then propose a greedy data-driven procedure that adaptively selects both interpolation frequencies and tangential directions. At every iteration, the frequency is chosen according to the largest transfer-function approximation error, while the tangential direction is selected from a dominant singular direction of the corresponding matrix-valued residual. Numerical experiments for wave propagation in lossy media demonstrate improved approximation efficiency compared with block adaptive interpolation. We further apply the method to spectral mass gauging of a three-dimensional propellant tank to provide an accurate estimate of the tank volume through Weyl's law.
item.dc:creator: Anarzhan Abilgazy, Mikhail Zaslavsky

item.title: Convergence analysis of TriCG and TriMR for symmetric quasi-definite linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: TriCG and TriMR are two short-recurrence iterative methods introduced by Montoison and Orban [SIAM J.\ Sci.\ Comput., 43 (2021), pp.\ A2502--A2525] for solving symmetric quasi-definite linear systems. Extensive numerical experiments have demonstrated the efficiency of these two methods, but a systematic convergence analysis is still lacking. In this paper, we derive convergence bounds for the TriCG error norm and the TriMR residual norm. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Kui Du, Jia-Jun Fan

item.title: A hybrid TT/QTT discontinuous Galerkin method with fixed-matrix upwinding for three-dimensional transient multigroup neutron transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.04360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a hybrid tensor-train/quantized tensor-train (TT/QTT) upwind discontinuous Galerkin method for three-dimensional transient multigroup neutron transport. The central contribution is a fixed-matrix upwind construction: two spatial DG matrices serve all directions and energy groups, with signed and absolute direction-cosine factors preserving Kronecker structure. For homogeneous materials on uniform Cartesian grids, operator rank bounds are independent of mesh size, group count and direction count at fixed scattering order. We derive a conditional global step-defect bound and enforce group-integrated balance of the compressed system. Crank-Nicolson tests show second-order convergence on a separable manufactured solution whose finest final state occupies 13 kB instead of 35 TB, a compression factor of $2.7\times10^9$. A modified rank-adaptive basis-update and Galerkin integrator (TT-BUG) advances passive and active bursts with approximately half a billion unknowns. Selected runs are 15-20 times faster than AMEn at comparable verified scalar-flux errors. In the reported anisotropic active-burst configurations, TT-BUG takes 14.3 s on one processor versus 716 s for OpenSn on 24 processors: approximately 50 times less wall time and 1200 times less allocated processor-time cost. This compares reported configurations rather than matched physical errors. OpenSn provides an independent discretization check. The modified TT-BUG source-onset and saturation treatment is tested numerically; its order, convergence and general tolerance-to-error relation remain unproved.
item.dc:creator: Dibyendu Adak, Radoslav Vuchkov, Oleg Korobkin, Ted Sariyski, Boian S. Alexandrov

item.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Approximation to a Class of Strongly Damped Wave Equations with Uniform Exponential Decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.04601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes and examines a completely discrete discontinuous Galerkin finite element scheme to approximate the solution of a class of strongly damped wave equations with uniform exponential decay property. In the first part, a semidiscrete discontinuous Galerkin approximation is employed in the spatial variable, while keeping time variable continuous and optimal error estimates are established while preserving the exponential decay property of the original system. Subsequently, a fully discrete scheme is developed and analyzed. Using suitable energy techniques, the consistency between the decay properties of the continuous and discrete systems is demonstrated. In particular, the constants appearing in various estimates remain uniformly bounded even as the damping parameters approach zero. Moreover, error estimates that preserve the uniform decay property are highlights of this paper. Further extension of our analysis includes a class of strongly damped fourth order evolution equations using SIPG as well as $C^0$-IP methods. Finally, several numerical experiments are performed to confirm the theoretical convergence results, verify the predicted decay behavior, and investigate the influence of model parameters on stability and computational accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Debendra K. Swain, P. Danumjaya, Anil Kumar, Amiya K. Pani

item.title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Framework for Efficient Simulation of Cyclic Voltammetry Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.04718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a numerical framework to efficiently simulate the cyclic voltammetry models based on discontinuous Galerkin (DG) spatial discretization combined with linearly implicit Euler time integration. The method is applied to two electrochemical mechanisms: a heterogeneous electron-transfer (ET) reaction and an electron-transfer reaction coupled with a catalytic chemical step (EC'). The governing time-dependent reaction-diffusion equations are expressed in dimensionless form and discretized in space using locally defined orthonormal Legendre polynomial basis functions. This discretization leads to a system of ordinary differential equations that is subsequently advanced in time using the linearly implicit Euler method. The resulting solver, denoted $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$, is evaluated through numerical experiments and compared with MATLAB's $pdepe$ solver in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The numerical results demonstrate the convergence of $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ with respect to spatial and temporal discretizations and show that the method accurately reproduces the voltammetric responses of both ET and EC' mechanisms. For a prescribed relative error, $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ requires less computational time than $pdepe$ in the numerical experiments considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DG formulation for the forward simulation of cyclic voltammetry models and provide a numerical foundation for subsequent adjoint-based parameter-estimation and inverse-problem formulations.
item.dc:creator: Assionvi Hove Kouevi, Debora Campos de Faria, Can Evren Yarman, Gabriel J. Lord

item.title: Generic factorizations and alternating direction method for fixed-rank approximation of matrix polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.04799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an algorithm for approximating a given matrix polynomial of degree $d$ by a matrix polynomial of prescribed rank and degree at most $d$. The method builds on recent advances in the theory of generic eigenstructures and factorizations of matrix polynomials with bounded rank and degree. We also give a specialized treatment of the case of matrix pencils (degree one matrix polynomials), motivated by its particular theoretical and practical importance. Lastly, numerical experiments are reported to assess the performance of the proposed approach and to compare it with existing methods.
item.dc:creator: Sweta Das, Andrii Dmytryshyn, Froil\'an M. Dopico, M{\aa}rten Gulliksson

item.title: Asymptotic preserving IMEX Active Flux schemes for a hyperbolic approximation of the Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a theoretical and numerical analysis of novel IMEX Active Flux schemes for a hyperbolic approximation of the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. For this approximation, it is important that the numerical schemes recover the limit equations (asymptotic preserving) and retain their order of accuracy in the limit (asymptotically accurate). Using formal asymptotic analysis and numerical experiments, we show that an Active Flux spatial discretisation (closely related to the standard semi-discrete Active Flux scheme), combined with an implicit-explicit Runge-Kutta scheme, is asymptotic preserving but not asymptotically accurate. We therefore propose alternative spatial discretisations that differ in the update equations of the point values. First, we derive a scheme by rescaling and eliminating terms in the upwind matrices. Second, we develop a second-order scheme by using central discretisation for the terms treated implicitly in time and present two modifications of it to third-order. Finally, we formulate a scheme with predefined upwind directions that are not chosen based on characteristics. We show that the alternative schemes are not only asymptotic preserving but also asymptotically accurate, and compare their accuracy, stability, and energy conservation numerically.
item.dc:creator: Simon Krotsch, Wasilij Barsukow, Christian Klingenberg

item.title: Marginalization-Based Regularization for Separable Nonlinear Least Squares Problems with Applications to Semi-Blind Deblurring
item.description: arXiv:2611.04846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Separable nonlinear least squares problems arise in inverse problems such as semi-blind image deblurring, where the image enters the forward model linearly, and the blur parameters enter nonlinearly. Even when the image is regularized, joint estimation of the image and blur parameters can favor a degenerate no-blur solution, in which the blur operator tends to the identity and the reconstruction merely denoises the data without removing the blur. We address this by regularizing the blur parameters. Motivated by the determinant term arising from Gaussian marginalization, we construct a family of blur-parameter priors whose weight and auxiliary operators can be chosen independently of the image prior. The resulting log-determinant penalty is incorporated into regularized variable projection, which eliminates the image variables by minimization. Under periodic boundary conditions and assuming the matrices involved admit a joint spectral decomposition, we show that a sufficiently large determinant weight rules out the no-blur solution as a local minimizer. We also characterize the regularizer's behavior as the auxiliary regularization scale tends to zero or infinity. We solve the reduced problem with a quasi-Newton method that evaluates the objective and its derivatives in the Fourier domain. In experiments with Gaussian, defocus, and motion blur, the proposed prior improves image and blur recovery over Gaussian marginalization across several settings, with determinant weights computed from the true image. A single-sample experiment illustrates how to automatically choose parameters from the data using a conditional generalized cross-validation criterion.
item.dc:creator: Jordan T. Dworaczyk, Malena I. Espa\~nol

item.title: A Compact Residual-Screened Local Reduced-Order Model for Diffuse-Domain Shape Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the compact residual-screened local reduced-order model (CL-ROM) from Brinkman-penalized flow to shape optimization with the diffuse domain method (DDM). As with Brinkman penalization, DDM extends evolving-domain problems to a fixed rectangular domain, allowing one grid for discretization and directly compatible snapshots from different designs. Unlike Brinkman penalization, DDM uses a phase field to weight operators and sources and treats Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin conditions through diffuse boundary terms. The CL-ROM mechanism carries over: recent full-order and corrected solutions determine local reduced spaces, while residual screening, correction with retained factors and objective verification decide when a full-order solve is needed. We derive reduced operators, residuals and sensitivities for each diffuse model, using Galerkin projection for the symmetric problems and least-squares Petrov--Galerkin projection for nonlinear flow. For the symmetric problems we prove a local approximation estimate that admits inexact, corrected snapshots. In numerical tests of shape identification, drag minimization in Navier--Stokes channel flow and compliance minimization of a cantilever, CL-ROM uses reduced solutions for nearly all design updates, reproduces the full-order objectives with relative differences below $5\times10^{-6}$, and is $3.85$ to $7.65$ times faster than a full-order baseline that reuses factorizations as preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoping Zhang, Anusooya Vasudevan, Lili Ju, Zhu Wang

item.title: Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Streamflow Models with Application to the Camastra Basin
item.description: arXiv:2611.04922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate streamflow estimation requires a consistent representation of model and observation uncertainty. Such consistency is difficult to obtain when rainfall information is unavailable, or not temporally aligned with the discharge observations. We develop an adaptive Kalman filter for Generalized Shot Noise streamflow models, with recursive estimation of the measurement and process-noise covariances. The process-noise update includes a correction for the covariance propagated through the state dynamics, without which the recursion has no finite stationary point. With the correction, the expected increment vanishes when the mean normalized innovation squared reaches one. The filter is assessed using 37 years of daily inflow observations from the Camastra Basin in southern Italy, under two rainfall configurations. The first supplies a synthetic effective-rainfall realization as a deterministic input, whereas the second represents the unresolved forcing through the adaptive process noise. The second configuration yields the more accurate estimates, since the synthetic rainfall events, although statistically calibrated, do not coincide in time with those that generated the observed discharge. Over the full record, it attains a Nash--Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.95 and a median relative error of about 1%. Regime-conditional consistency diagnostics are reported and discussed for the second configuration.
item.dc:creator: Mario Pezzella, Luigi Cimorelli, Luisa D'Amore, Salvatore Cuomo

item.title: Nonlinear SBP operators for stable approximations of skew-symmetric hyperbolic initial boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators in combination with simultaneous-approximation-terms (SATs) for boundary conditions provides a recipe that can be applied to well posed linear initial boundary value problems.The SBP-SAT frame work guarantees semi-discrete energy stability and can be applied to most numerical discretization methods. High order accuracy comes without additional difficulty. The extension of SBP-SAT to nonlinear initial boundary value problems has so far been somewhat unclear. However, recent developments have shown how to construct stable nonlinear SAT terms. In this note we develop nonlinear SBP operators. These combined developments provide an SBP-SAT based recipe for stable approximations of nonlinear skew-symmetric hyperbolic initial boundary value problems.
item.dc:creator: Jan Nordstr\"om

item.title: A Unified Isoparametric Moving Mesh PDE Method for P1 and Q1 Elements with Certified Local Nonsingularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.05026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified isoparametric moving mesh partial differential equation (MMPDE) method for $P_1$ simplicial and $Q_1$ tensor-product elements, including elements on embedded surfaces. Mesh movement follows a prescribed symmetric positive-definite metric through equidistribution and alignment. For $Q_1$ elements, we prove that bounded, exactly integrated adaptation energy prevents local Jacobian rank loss on a fixed finite mesh at sharp critical exponents. The result also gives local full-rank preservation for embedded bilinear surface elements. A complete physical-coordinate gradient accounts for metric variation at moving quadrature points. For the discrete MMPDE, we use whole-element validity tests and develop sufficient Bernstein certificates for trilinear hexahedra. An explicit positive-margin bound on each fixed stage is provided by an optional certificate barrier. Numerical examples illustrate metric-driven movement on one-dimensional, planar, volume, and graph-surface meshes. Limitations of pointwise hexahedral Jacobian sampling are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Xianping Li

item.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.05211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model reduction via the Mori-Zwanzig (MZ) formalism is well understood for coarse-grained representations constructed from standard basis functions such as Fourier functions. We show that the same formalism can be used to build reduced-order models in bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning. The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) is used to close the resulting non-Markovian evolution equations for the expansion coefficients of the learned basis. We further introduce a complementary, generative closure model. Relative to the Markovian dynamics alone, both the MZ and generative closures substantially improve predictions of the filtered states.
item.dc:creator: Emily Williams, Saad Qadeer, Amanda Howard, Panos Stinis

item.title: CQ-collocation BEMs for exterior wave propagation problems: the 3D Neumann case
item.description: arXiv:2611.05226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider three-dimensional exterior wave propagation problems with non-homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We reformulate the problem as a space-time boundary integral equation involving a hypersingular operator. To solve the resulting formulation, we combine Lubich's convolution quadrature with a shifted collocation boundary element discretization and investigate numerically the efficiency, stability, and convergence of the resulting numerical scheme. Numerical tests show that the proposed approach achieves an accuracy comparable to that of Lubich's convolution quadrature combined with a Galerkin boundary element method, and provide numerical evidence of the unconditional stability of the collocation scheme.
item.dc:creator: Davide Collato, Silvia Falletta, Giovanni Monegato, Letizia Scuderi

item.title: Remap for ALE Hydrodynamics via Direct Interpolation and Constraint Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.05327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents an optimization-based remap approach for arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) hydrodynamics that preserves sharp features and physical bounds while conserving global quantities such as volume, mass, momentum, and total energy. Achieving these properties is the main challenge in remap methods. The presented approach is well-suited for high-order finite element (FE) discretizations and ALE methods that allow for large, purely Lagrangian displacements between successive remeshing and remapping steps. Recent advances in parallel, GPU-capable interpolation routines enable the initial transfer of all fields via direct physical-space interpolation, avoiding computationally costly and diffusive pseudo-transient PDE-based advection. The interpolation produces bounded fields with minimal numerical diffusion. However, it may violate the desired conservation of global properties. Thus, a subsequent optimization step restores conservation while preserving physical bounds. The presented method provides minimally diffusive remapping of finite element fields of arbitrary order. Moreover, it directly remaps quantities defined at integration points, eliminating the need for projection onto finite element spaces. The approach also mitigates typical challenges associated with synchronizing primal variables and conserved quantities in advection-based remap methods. The proposed optimization-based remap method is evaluated using standard two- and three-dimensional remap benchmarks and full ALE hydrodynamics simulations.
item.dc:creator: Brendan Keith, Dohyun Kim, Boyan Lazarov, Ketan Mittal, Cosmin G. Petra, Mathias R. Schmidt, Vladimir Z. Tomov

item.title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
item.description: arXiv:2611.05365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/\Delta t$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $\Delta t$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. Our remedy needs no FP64 arithmetic: each state variable is stored as the unevaluated sum of two FP32 numbers, updated with error-free transformations, while every right-hand-side evaluation stays in FP32. Unlike compensated summation, it needs no rewriting of the scheme. In model problems from geophysical flow, mechanical dynamics and celestial mechanics, with five Runge-Kutta and multistep schemes, it restores design-order convergence to the floor. In large-eddy simulations of a high-lift airplane wing on three refined grids, up to 544 million cells, with time steps $\Delta t$, $\Delta t/2$ and $\Delta t/4$, FP32 overpredicts the lift by 2.1, 4.5 and 7.7%, while the two-float lift agrees with FP64 within 0.3% on every grid, and on graphics processing units the production solver runs 1.6 to 2.7 times faster than FP64.
item.dc:creator: Michael F. Barad

item.title: Multi-modal Laplace-based sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.03773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the multi-modal Laplace approximation, given by a weighted Gaussian mixture centred at the local minima of the negative log-density, for sampling from probability measures that concentrate around finitely many modes as an inverse-temperature parameter $n$ grows. Such distributions occur in Bayesian inference in the small noise or large data regime. We derive explicit, non-asymptotic bounds on the Hellinger distance between the multi-modal Laplace approximation and the concentrating posterior. The bound decays like $n^{-1/2}$ with $n$ and the constants depend only polynomially on the dimension $d$. Moreover, we analyse the Laplace mixture as a proposal distribution for self-normalised importance sampling and independent Metropolis--Hastings (IMH) targeting concentration multimodal distributions. We derive asymptotic results, as $n\to\infty$, on the effective sample size in case of importance sampling as well as on the average acceptance probability, lag-one autocorrelation, and spectral gap in case of IMH. Numerical experiments illustrate and verify our theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Eg\'ea, Hanyue Gu, Daniel Rudolf, Bj\"orn Sprungk

item.title: The obstacle problem for fractional heat equations with memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.04971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the obstacle problem for the evolution equation $\partial_t^\alpha u+(-\Delta)^s u=0$ in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $\partial_t^\alpha$ with $\alpha\in(0,1)$ is the Caputo derivative in time and $(-\Delta)^s$ with $s\in(0,1]$ is the fractional Laplacian in space ($s<1$) or the classical Laplacian ($s=1$). We prove that the problem has at most one bounded viscosity solution, and we obtain existence as the limit of an explicit monotone finite-difference scheme, which combines the L1 discretization of the Caputo derivative with powers of the discrete Laplacian. The scheme is also used to establish regularity estimates in space and time. We then study the large-time behaviour: solutions converge, along subsequences, to stationary solutions, and we identify the limit when the initial datum coincides with the obstacle (the minimal stationary solution) or has a limit $c_*$ at infinity. In the latter case the dimension plays a role, as a consequence of the recurrence of the underlying process: the limit is the unique stationary solution with limit $c_*$ at infinity if $d>2s$, and a constant (the maximum between $c_*$ and the supremum of the obstacle) if $d\le2s$. Numerical experiments in one dimension, based on an explicit stationary solution, illustrate the convergence of the scheme and the relaxation towards the stationary profile.
item.dc:creator: F\'elix del Teso, Fernando Quir\'os, Julio D. Rossi

item.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fr\'echet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Gracyk

item.title: Extracting Dual Analytic Geometries of Linear Transformations to Achieve Efficient Computation
item.description: arXiv:2506.11990v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalize the Calderon-Zygmund methodology for operator analysis and the Rokhlin-Greengard fast multipole algorithms, in which the domain and range of an operator are jointly organized. Our methods analyze unstructured kernels by uncovering the joint hidden geometries of their domain and range. The main tool is the Questionnaire algorithm, an iterative procedure that constructs adaptive bi-hierarchical partition trees that reveal latent multiscale organization and local low-rank structure in the kernel. When the geometry is unknown, the iteration starts from any initial affinity, even a random one, and, with a stochastic flip perturbation and a spectral space-filling curve that fixes the left-right order of every tree, reorganizes the matrix into an image of the operator's "phase space": the joint space of its sources and sensors, in duality, as positions and frequencies are for the Fourier transform. This ordering gives the phase space an analytic structure on which any classical transform can be carried out; the resulting compression is direct evidence of that structure. Guided by these geometries, we obtain efficient factorizations and fast matrix-vector products in two ways: (1) the Butterfly algorithm, which exploits the learned bi-hierarchical localized low-rank structure; and (2) the adaptive eGHWT, which selects best tilings in space and sequency from all levels of generalized Haar-Walsh wavelet packets. We call the resulting algorithms the Questionnaire Factorization and Fast Transform (QFFT). Unlike classical approaches requiring prior knowledge of the geometry, QFFT is fully data-driven and applies to matrices from irregular or unknown distributions. We demonstrate it on heterogeneous oscillatory operators and on orthogonal eigenvector expansions with high multiplicity and random sampling, reducing storage from O(N^2) to O(N log N) and enabling fast, scalable computation.
item.dc:creator: Pei-Chun Su, Ronald R. Coifman

item.title: A posteriori analysis of neural network approximations of partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2507.06017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With the aim of defining robust losses for the neural network approximation of partial differential equations, we study, in a general setting, a posteriori estimates used in finite element analysis. We show that the error is equivalent to the sum of two residuals provided that the underlying variational formulation is well-posed. The first contribution is the projection of the residual to a finite-dimensional space and is therefore computable, while the second one can be reliably estimated by a computable upper bound in many practical scenarios. Two important applications can be considered during the neural network optimization (training) process: first, the computable lower bound is used as loss functional and both contributions are used to monitor the error at each solver step; or second, the two estimators are included in the loss functional, thereby providing total control over the error. As a model problem, we consider a second-order elliptic partial differential equation and discuss several variational formulations, including different approaches for incorporating boundary conditions into the estimators. Various numerical experiments are presented to validate our findings.
item.dc:creator: Thomas F\"uhrer, Sergio Rojas

item.title: Finite Element Complexes with Trace Structures: A unified framework for cohomology and bounded interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2509.23788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a unified framework for studying the cohomology and constructing $L^2$-bounded commuting interpolation operators for finite element complexes, such as the Hessian, divdiv, elasticity and Stokes complexes. Compared with the standard de Rham complex, these complexes present additional challenges arising from algebraic constraints on tensor fields, such as symmetry and tracelessness, as well as additional smoothness requirements. The main ingredient of our framework is a direct sum decomposition of finite element complexes into skeletal and bubble parts. To establish this decomposition, we introduce two key structures: trace structures and generalized currents. In this decomposition, the bubble part is characterized by bubble complexes associated with subsimplices of different dimensions, including vertices, edges, and faces. We prove that the exactness of the resulting bubble complexes ensures that the finite element complex has the correct cohomology. Based on this decomposition, we further construct $L^2$-bounded interpolation operators for these finite element complexes.
item.dc:creator: Jun Hu, Yizhou Liang, Ting Lin

item.title: An efficient boundary integral equation solution technique for solving aperiodic scattering problems from two-dimensional, periodic boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2511.04424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This manuscript presents an efficient boundary integral equation technique for solving two-dimensional Helmholtz problems defined in the half-plane bounded by an infinite, periodic curve with Neumann boundary conditions and with an aperiodic point source. The technique is designed for boundaries where one period does not require a large number of discretization points to achieve high accuracy. The inverse Floquet--Bloch transform turns the problem into evaluating a contour integral where the integrand is the solution of quasiperiodic boundary value problems. To approximate the integral, one must solve a collection of these problems. This manuscript uses a variant of the periodizing scheme by Cho and Barnett which avoids using the quasiperiodic Green's function in the integral representation and is amenable to a large amount of precomputation that can be reused for all the necessary solves. The solution technique is accelerated using low rank linear algebra and corner compression. The performance of the method is measured on a range of simple and complex boundary geometries, including in the presence of one or more corners with straight or curved edges present in the unit cell. The numerical results illustrate that the presented method is competitive with techniques using the quasiperiodic Green's function kernel for smooth boundaries, and up to 20--30 faster when corner compression and high accuracy is required.
item.dc:creator: Riley Fisher, Fruzsina Agocs, Adrianna Gillman

item.title: Decoupled energy-stable Runge-Kutta schemes of arbitrary order for the anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth model
item.description: arXiv:2606.25345v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces a novel and general framework for constructing arbitrary-order, energy-stable, and decoupled schemes for the anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth model. The proposed framework combines a time-dependent auxiliary variable, an algebraically stable Runge-Kutta method, and a matrix diagonalization technique. This unique combination yields a scheme that is proven to be unconditionally energy-dissipative while requiring only the solution of independent, constant-coefficient elliptic equations at each time step, which can be solved in parallel. The auxiliary variable is recovered from a uniquely solvable $q\times q$ algebraic system. We provide a rigorous proof of $q$th-order convergence in time for a $q$-stage Runge-Kutta method within a fixed Fourier-Galerkin space. Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D not only confirm the theoretical convergence and energy stability but also demonstrate the efficiency of the decoupled approach and provide a detailed investigation of key parameters' effects on dendritic morphology.
item.dc:creator: Weiwen Wang, Chuanju Xu, Shaoqin Zheng

item.title: Automated Numerical Stability Analysis of Deep Learning Operators
item.description: arXiv:2607.25494v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finite-precision arithmetic unavoidably introduces numerical approximation errors. Numerical computations may use insufficient precision or an improper formulation, which leads to numerical instability. In this paper, we introduce a unified software tool for stochastic numerical validation of deep-learning operators. The tool follows CESTAC on supported exposed operations and uses an operator-level data-perturbation approximation for GEMM-like kernels. Our developed software not only enables numerical validation with a single computation pass but also detects the sources of numerical instability and provides numerical stability monitoring during deep learning training and inference. We verified its effectiveness on the detection of polluted operators with injected numerical instabilities across various tasks. We believe that our developed method and tools provide valuable insights into developing numerically stable computing kernels, which are particularly critical for numerically stable and efficient deep learning training and inference.
item.dc:creator: Xinye Chen

item.title: Isogeometric analysis for the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.21862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The transmission eigenvalue problem plays an increasingly important role in inverse scattering theory. Although significant progress has been made in developing efficient numerical methods for the problem over the last two decades, its numerical treatment for curved domains in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2,3$) remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce and analyze a geometrically flexible and $H^2$-conforming isogeometric method for solving a fourth-order, quadratic and non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problem arising from the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem. Using the spectral approximation theory for compact non-self-adjoint operators, we derive optimal error estimates for the discrete eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. Numerical results for the two- and three-dimensional benchmark problems, including those defined in curved domains, are presented to verify our theoretical results, and to demonstrate the advantages of the method over existing numerical methods in terms of both accuracy and geometric flexibility.
item.dc:creator: Nizheng Liao, Guanghui Hu, Xucheng Meng

item.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.08701v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the probability that Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting on $n \times n$ Gaussian random matrices has growth $\rho$ is at least inverse quasi-polynomial: $\Omega\left(\exp\left(-c \log^2 \left(\frac{\rho}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\log(n)\right)\right)$ for some constant $c > 0$. In particular, the probability of growth $\rho \ge n^{1/2 + \epsilon}$ is at least $\exp(- O (\epsilon^2 \log^3 (n) ))$. This lower bound breaks standard conjectures in the smoothed and average-case analysis of Gaussian elimination. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first non-trivial lower bound on the probability of large growth for Gaussian random matrices.
item.dc:creator: Daniel A. Spielman, Xifan Yu

item.title: CutIGA with Least Squares Stabilized Nitsche Boundary Conditions: The Biharmonic Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.11636v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a symmetric Nitsche method for the biharmonic Dirichlet problem on a smooth domain whose boundary may cut arbitrarily through the computational mesh. Bulk least-squares stabilization in a boundary strip and tangential boundary penalties control the consistency terms through an explicit lifting of the two Dirichlet traces. This gives coercivity on $H^4(\Omega)$ without inverse inequalities and permits a fixed penalty independent of the cut configuration for sufficiently thin strips. Under suitable regularity assumptions, splines of degree $p\geq4$ give energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{p-1}$ and $h^{p+1}$. We also analyze a face-stabilized extension to $C^1$ splines of degree $p=2$ and $C^2$ splines of degree $p=3$. Exact-ellipse experiments examine convergence, cut stability, and parameter sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Mats G. Larson, Karl Larsson

item.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.41715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Tianyang Chu, Mingyan Zhang

item.title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.01448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain \Omega in \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (\Delta t=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: Optimal L^2 Error Estimates for CSLDG Ideal Numerical Solutions in Time-Dependent Compressible Periodic Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.02867v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the characteristic Galerkin-type semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element (CSLDG) method for conservative linear transport equations. When the characteristic maps and upstream regions are exact, each update of the ideal CSLDG scheme is equivalent to exact conservative transport of the current numerical solution followed by L^2 projection onto the background DG space. The conventional estimate obtained by accumulating projection errors over successive time steps loses one order when \Delta t\asymp h, but this loss does not represent the actual accuracy of the scheme. For smooth velocity fields \A(\x,t) on a common periodic lattice, we construct local correctors used only in the analysis on uniform Cartesian meshes, assuming that \Delta t/h is fixed and that every component of the local Courant vector remains uniformly separated from the integers throughout the space-time domain. We prove strict contraction of the reference-cell transport-projection operator on the zero-mean polynomial space, establish uniform solvability of the corrector equation and Lipschitz estimates with respect to its parameter, and control the difference between the exact flow map and a local frozen translation through weak integral moments. This yields a one-step residual of order O(h^{K+2}), and, while retaining the step-by-step update and the standard L^2-projected initial data, gives, for the P^K approximation, an optimal O(h^{K+1}) error bound. The velocity may depend on both space and time, and incompressibility is not required. An appendix extends the analysis to a compact-support setting, in which the velocity field and the solution need not share a common spatial period.
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: On the growth of the parameters of approximating ReLU neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2406.14936v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work focuses on the analysis of fully connected feed forward ReLU neural networks as they approximate a given, smooth function. In contrast to conventionally studied universal approximation properties under increasing architectures, e.g., in terms of width or depth of the networks, we are concerned with the asymptotic growth of the parameters of approximating networks. Such results are of interest, e.g., for error analysis or consistency results for neural network training. The main result of our work is that, for a ReLU architecture with state of the art approximation error, the realizing parameters grow at most polynomially. The obtained rate with respect to a normalized network size is compared to existing results and is shown to be superior in most cases, in particular for high dimensional input.
item.dc:creator: Erion Morina, Martin Holler

item.title: Path-Kernel Method for Differentiating Unstable Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2503.00718v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive and rigorously prove the path-kernel formula for the linear response of stochastic differential equations, namely, the derivative of averaged statistics with respect to a model parameter. The parameter may affect the diffusion coefficient, as well as the drift coefficient and initial condition. No hyperbolicity assumption is required. The proof introduces a single change of variables for the state path that transfers part of the unstable path perturbation to differentiation of the probability kernel. We also derive a pathwise Monte Carlo algorithm for estimating the response and demonstrate it on the 40-dimensional noisy Lorenz--96 system.
item.dc:creator: Angxiu Ni

item.title: Data-Efficient Kernel Methods for Learning Differential Equations and Their Solution Operators: Algorithms and Error Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2503.01036v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a novel kernel-based framework for learning differential equations and their solution maps. The framework is efficient in its data requirements in terms of the number of observed states and the amount of data available per state. Our formulation also allows us to employ efficient Gauss-Newton-type optimization algorithms in the training procedure to improve accuracy and speed of the training procedure. We also support our algorithm with rigorous theoretical guarantees in the form of quantitative worst-case error bounds for the learned equation that can be extended to the subsequent solution operators under smoothness assumptions. Numerical benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements in computational complexity and robustness while achieving one to two orders of magnitude improvements in terms of accuracy compared to certain state-of-the-art algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Bamdad Hosseini, Alexander Hsu, Yasamin Jalalian, Juan Felipe Osorio Ramirez, Houman Owhadi

item.title: Exact Gaussian Moment Matching for Residual Networks: a Second-Order Method
item.description: arXiv:2601.22307v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of propagating the mean and covariance of a general multivariate Gaussian distribution through a deep (residual) neural network using layer-by-layer moment matching. We close a longstanding gap by deriving exact moment matching for the probit, GeLU, ReLU (as a limit of GeLU), Heaviside (as a limit of probit), and sine activation functions; for both feedforward and generalized residual layers. On large-variance random networks, median KL-divergence improvements over common baselines range from tens to thousands of times. On a variational Bayes neural network, we show that our method improves upon a state-of-the-art deterministic inference method by an order of magnitude in KL divergence from Monte Carlo ground truth. We also give a smooth-distance error bound showing that, under regularity assumptions, moment matching removes the leading low-variance errors and propagates higher-order local accuracy through the layers of a network.
item.dc:creator: Simon Kuang, Xinfan Lin

item.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.
item.dc:creator: Zixi Yi, Gary P. T. Choi
